safetyNote: Deadly poisonous: Lepiota subincarnata contains amatoxins. Serious vomiting and diarrhoea may start only after a symptom-free delay, followed by potentially fatal liver damage. Never taste or eat it. Seek emergency medical advice immediately after suspected ingestion, even if you feel well.

sections.title: Fatal dapperling
sections.text: Lepiota subincarnata is a small pinkish dapperling. The cap is usually about 1.5–6 cm across, initially convex and later flatter with a low central bump. A pink-brown velvety layer breaks into small, sometimes concentric, scales over a paler cream or flesh-coloured background; the centre stays darker and more felted. Colour, cap size and scale pattern vary substantially between specimens.

sections.title: Gills, stem and veil
sections.text: The white to pale-cream gills are free from the stem and relatively close; the spore print is white. The slender pale stem is commonly about 1.5–5.5 cm long. Pink-brown fleecy bands or scales mark its lower part, while the upper part is smoother. The upper veil remnant is usually a faint, fragile woolly ring zone rather than a prominent persistent skirt and may be absent. A sweet or fruity smell is possible but can be indistinct, so it is not a dependable test.

sections.title: Habitat, names and confusion
sections.text: This saprotrophic mushroom grows in gardens, lawns, parks, woodland clearings and leaf litter, usually in summer and autumn. Some taxonomic authorities treat Lepiota josserandii as a synonym of L. subincarnata, although other authors distinguish similar forms. It has been fatally mistaken for the fairy ring mushroom, Marasmius oreades, in a lawn. The edible species usually has a smooth tan cap and tough stem, but field identification must never rest on one feature.

sections.title: Amatoxin poisoning
sections.text: Like the death cap, this species can cause the phalloid syndrome. A symptom-free period of at least several hours is followed by abdominal pain, vomiting and watery diarrhoea; liver injury can then develop even if symptoms briefly ease. A documented British Columbia case began after about 13 hours and was fatal. Do not wait for symptoms or use any supposed safe quantity threshold: suspected ingestion requires immediate emergency or poison-centre advice.

sections.title: About the plate
sections.text: The white-background plate shows a whole mushroom, a longitudinal section, the scaled cap from above and the free-gilled underside. The narrow fleecy ring zone and pink-brown lower-stem bands are visible without suggesting that the veil is always prominent.
